## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
# Project URL https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/avikpaul4u/vehicle-loan-default-prediction?select=train.csv


# Load our files (saved manually to data directory)
# Training data
train_dat = read.csv('./data/train.csv')

# Testing data (DO NOT LOAD UNTIL WEEK 8 OR 9!!)
#test_dat = read.csv('./data/test.csv')

head(train_dat)
str(train_dat)

training <- 


sample <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), nrow(train_dat), replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.7,0.3))
train  <- train_dat[sample, ]
test   <- train_dat[!sample, ]

test
  

```

```{r}
# Check for any columns with missing data
sapply(train_dat, anyNA)
```




You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
